_about: Tie-breaks between Sports-Reference (sr, what the app shows) and the uconnhuskies.com schedule cards (official) for disputed game facts. truth = adjudicated value; winner = sr | official | neither. Sources are independent of both where possible (opponent archives/media guides, AP agate & roundups via International Herald Tribune and other newspapers on archive.org, CNN/SI-STATS box scores via the Wayback Machine, ESPN). uconn_record_book = what UConn's own 2026-27 record book (all-time results) shows, for context: many web-card typos are absent there, a few originate there.

sources.quote: Sat Nov 25 vs. UConn Anchorage, Alaska L Loss 81-95
Nov. 25—Connecticut 95, Auburn 81
Nov. 25: Connecticut 95, Auburn 81

decisions.note: Auburn (schedule + media guide), host UAA's Shootout history and UConn's record book all give 81, and UConn's official 1989-90 opponent total (2,446) only reconciles with 81. Caveat: the AP agate printed in the IHT of Nov 27, 1989 reads 'Connecticut 95, Auburn 91' - probably SR's source; treated as a wire typo.

A vacation of records in which men's basketball student-athletes competed while ineligible.

Wikipedia's claim that no 2016-17 games were vacated is wrong per the NCAA book.
